title: The Plaza Hotel is closing at the start of 2027, leaving wedding plans in limbo
text:
The iconic New York City hotel is set to undergo years of repairs that, if completed on schedule, could take four years.
The iconic New York City hotel is set to undergo years of repairs that, if completed on schedule, could take four years. The Plaza Hotel is checking out for four years, all part of a major makeover.
Work will take years, which is why it’s closing, but 180 luxury apartments won’t be affected from the constant construction. So what will be changing for the famous midtown hotel? NBC New York’s Andrew Siff reports. The Plaza Hotel, located across Central Park at 5th Avenue and 59th Street, is set to undergo repairs of its historic facade.
The restoration work is said to be so extensive that the entire hotel needs to shut down for roughly four years to complete the necessary repairs. The 119-year-old hotel is currently scheduled to close down in January of 2027. If construction is done on schedule, it should reopen in 2031. The hotel has a facade that the city has deemed unsafe, according to schematics obtained by NBC New York.
The Department of Buildings said photos showed evidence of unsafe conditions. New city laws would allow $6,000 monthly fines to begin in January, which the hotel is looking to avoid. But the repairs are complicated, as a spokesperson said the work involves"careful consideration given to preservation requirements and the building’s long-term care, as well as the safety of our guests, employees, and the wider community.
" New York City Councilwoman Virginia Maloney, who represents the district, said there are other complications as well. "I’ve heard there’s only one or two suppliers that can provide the materials needed to modernize the facade," Maloney said. It's not yet clear how the upcoming closure will impact the substantial wedding operations. The 180 luxury apartments in the building won't have to be vacated while the repairs are being done.
Nearly 400 people work at the hotel as doormen, porters and maintenance staff — who could go without pay while the fixes are being done.
"I am concerned about the workers who will get health care and benefits but likely to be without wages for the entire duration," said Manhattan Borough President Brad Hoylman-Sigal. The landmark 18-story hotel, first opened in 1907, has been popularized many times over in film and television -- perhaps most famously in"Home Alone 2: Lost in New York.
" It is on the National Register of Historic Places. Since opening, the hotel has gone through a number of renovations. It is currently home to 282 guestrooms and 181 condo units.
